title: Aaron and Hur Hold Up Moses' Arms
text:
In the Book of Exodus, soon after the Israelites left Egypt, the people of Amalek attacked them at Rephidim. Moses told Joshua to choose men and go out to fight. He himself would stand on top of the hill with the staff of God in his hand.

The next day Joshua led the fighting in the valley, and Moses climbed the hill with his brother Aaron and with Hur. As long as Moses held up his hands, Israel prevailed. Whenever he lowered them, Amalek prevailed.

But as the hours went on, Moses' arms grew heavy. He could not keep them raised. So Aaron and Hur took a stone and put it under him, and he sat on it. Then they stood on either side of him, one on one side and one on the other, and held up his hands. His hands stayed steady until the sun went down.

In the valley below, Joshua's men defeated Amalek.
lesson: Even the strongest leader tires, and no one can hold the line alone all day. Good teammates notice when someone is flagging and quietly hold up their arms.
